translations.text: [?] his day comes, when he must die.
For as soon as the soul sets out on its journey and leaves the body lying, a host comes from the stars of heaven, and another from the pitch [of hell]. There they fight over it.
The soul may worry until the judgment comes, which of the two hosts it will be fetched by.
For if Satan's company wins it, they lead it at once to where it will suffer, into fire and into darkness. That is a truly terrible thing.
But if those who come from heaven fetch it, and it becomes the property of the angels, they bring it at once up into the kingdom of heaven.
There is life without death, light without darkness, a dwelling without sorrow. No one there is sick.
When a man wins a dwelling in paradise, a house in heaven, help enough comes to him there.
Therefore every man has great need for his mind to urge him to do God's will gladly and to shun hell's fire, the torment of pitch, with all his strength.
There Satan, the ancient one, offers hot flame. So anyone who knows himself to be sinful may think about this and worry greatly.
Woe to him who must atone for his crimes in darkness and burn in pitch. It is a truly baleful thing when a man cries out to God and no help comes to him.
The wretched soul hopes for mercy, but it is not in the mind of the heavenly God, because here in the world it did not work for it.
When the mighty king summons the assembly, every kindred must come there. Then no child dares to ignore the summons, nor may any man [fail to come] to the assembly.
There he must stand before the ruler to give account for whatever he had ever done in the world.
I heard men learned in worldly law say that the Antichrist must fight with Elijah.
The outlaw is armed. Then battle will break out between them.
The champions are so mighty, and the stake is so great.
Elijah fights for eternal life and wants to strengthen the kingdom for the righteous. Therefore he who rules heaven will help him.
The Antichrist stands with the old fiend, with Satan, who will drag him down. Therefore he will fall wounded on the battlefield and be defeated on that journey.
Yet many men of God believe that Elijah will be wounded in that fight.

When Elijah's blood drips onto the earth, the mountains will burn, not a single tree will stand anywhere on earth, the waters will dry up, the marsh will swallow itself, the sky will smoulder with flame,

the moon will fall, middle-earth will burn, no stone will stay standing. Then the day of punishment will go into the land, go with fire to visit men. There no kinsman can help another before the Muspilli.
When the broad earth all burns up, and fire and air sweep it all away, where then is the borderland where a man always fought alongside his kinsmen?
The borderland is burnt up, and the soul stands oppressed and does not know how to atone. So it goes to punishment.
Therefore it is very good for a man, when he comes to the assembly, to have judged every case rightly.
Then he need not worry when he comes to the judgment.
The wretched man does not know what guardian he has when he obstructs what is right with bribes, and that the devil stands hidden by him there.
He keeps a record of every matter, of whatever evil the man did before and since, so that he will tell all of it when the man comes to the judgment. So no man should ever accept bribes.
When the heavenly horn is sounded, and he who is to judge sets out on his journey, then the greatest of hosts rises with him. It is all so bold that no one can contend with him.
Then he goes to the place of assembly that has been marked out there. There the judgment takes place that people have always spoken of.
Then angels travel across the lands, waking the peoples and summoning them to the assembly.
Then every man shall rise from the dust,
free himself from the burden of the grave mound. His body shall come back to him, so that he may plead his whole case and be judged according to his deeds.
When he who is to judge, and to judge the dead and the living, takes his seat, then a multitude of angels and of good men stands around him there.
The court is so great; so many come there to the judgment, rising from their rest, that no man can escape anything there.
There the hand shall speak, the head shall tell, and every one of the limbs, down to the little finger, what murder he committed among these people.
There is no man so cunning that he can lie about anything there, or hide any of his deeds,
so that it will not all be made known before the king, unless he has forestalled [?] it with alms and atoned for the crimes with fasting.
Then he who has atoned can be confident.
Then the Lord's cross, on which holy Christ was hanged, is carried forward.
Then he shows the wounds which he [received] in his human form, which he [?] for the love of this human race [?]
